title: Protocol for indirect and direct co-culture between human cancer cells and endothelial cells
protocol: Pre-warm the media, PBS, and trypsin in a 37°C water bath.
Clean the cell culture hood and turn on UV light for 30 min before the experiment starts.
Check the cell status and ensure confluences reach about 80%–90%.
Remove media and wash cells using warm PBS once.
Incubate cells with trypsin for 2 min to detach them from the dish.
Add medium to trypsin in a 2:1 ratio (medium:trypsin) to neutralize the trypsin.
Centrifuge cells at 200–300 × g for 5 min at room temperature (22°C–27°C).
Discard the medium and re-suspend cells with 2 ml medium for cell counting.
Seed 2 ml cancer cells with a density of 3.0 × 10^5 cells/mL in each well of a 6-well plate.
Prepare a second 6-well plate by carefully placing the transwell inserts in the 6-well plate.
Ensure that the insert does not just stand in the well but fits properly with a gap between it and the well.
Seed cells onto the transwell inserts for the experimental group HMVECi-D.
Use BON or MCF-7 cells as control groups on the inserts.
Culture the seeded cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours before starting the co-culture.
Seed MCF-7 and BON cells in a 6-well plate for 24 h (Day 1).
Culture both cancer cells and HMVECi-D cells in inserts in a second well plate for 24 h (Day 1).
Change the media after 24 h of culture.
Add inserts to 6-well plates containing only cancer cells on Day 2.
Aspirate the medium in the 6-well plate and transwell insert on Day 2.
Replace endothelial cell medium with cancer cell medium.
Wash cancer cells twice with PBS after 48 h co-culture.
Lysis of cells to collect total RNA using RNeasy Mini Kit Protocol.
Quantify RNA concentration by Nanodrop.
Dilute samples with molecular biology-grade water as needed to maintain equal concentrations.
Prepare mixture for reverse transcription in PCR tubes following the recipe.
Dilute fibrinogen powder in DPBS without Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺ to a concentration of 20 mg/mL.
Calculate the amount of fibrinogen needed for each ring, based on the volume required (50 μl per ring).
Dilute fibrinogen powder with DPBS outside the hood.
Incubate the tube containing fibrinogen in a 37°C water bath for at least 1 hour.
Spin the tube at 8–10 × g for 2 minutes at room temperature (22°C–27°C).
Sterile filter the fibrinogen using a syringe and a 0.22 μm low-retention filter in the cell culture hood.
Return the filtered fibrinogen to the 37°C water bath to keep warm while harvesting cells.
Pre-warm endothelial cell medium, BON cell medium, CAF medium, trypsin, PBS, and DPBS.
Spray 70% ethanol to clean the hood and turn on UV light to sterilize the entire cell culture hood for at least 30 minutes.
Transfer PDMS rings on coverslips into each well of a 24-well plate in the tissue culture hood.
Harvest cells by detaching and collecting all the cells in a 50 mL tube.
Take 10 μL for cell counting.
Resuspend BON, HMEC-1, and CAF cells at appropriate densities following Table 8.
Count the number of cells harvested for each cell line.
Calculate the volume of medium required to dilute the cells to reach the needed concentration for the ring assay.
Prepare cell suspensions in sterile microcentrifuge tubes for loading rings.
Ensure that BON, HMEC-1, and CAF cell confluence values are 80%–90% in each 10 cm dish.
Mix BON, HMEC-1 and CAF cell suspensions (22 μL for each cell type).
Add 9 μL of thrombin to the mixed cell suspension.
Thoroughly mix the cell suspension with thrombin.
Combine 75 μL of fibrinogen into the cell-thrombin mixture via pipette trituration three times.
Quickly change the pipette volume from 75 μL to 50 μL and add 50 μL to each ring.
Avoid introducing bubbles while adding the solution.
Mix fibrinogen three times using a 75 μL pipette.
With the dispensing button depressed, swirl the pipette tip around to fully spread the gel mix throughout the whole ring.
Transfer 50 μL of the mixture to each ring.
Swirl the solutions in each ring to ensure even dispersion.
Move quickly to complete three rings within 30 seconds.
Move the completed rings to an incubator and allow the gels to set for up to 30 minutes.
Do not let the gel sit for more than one hour before adding medium; any longer compromises gel stability and may cause cell death.
Add 1 mL of EGM-2 medium into the wells containing the mixture of BON, HMEC, and CAF cells.
Check the cell status daily and change the media every two days.
Culture the cells for a total of seven days before proceeding to step 32.
Remove the 24-well plate with rings from the incubator and transfer to a lab bench for histological analysis.
Wash the rings with approximately 500 μl PBS twice, each for 5 min.
Use a vacuum aspirator flask on the bench to aspirate the media from the 24-well plate.
Fix rings using 10% formalin for 20 minutes on an orbital shaker at room temperature (22°C–27°C).
Remove 10% formalin by pipette and dispose according to hazardous waste protocols.
Wash the rings with PBS on an orbital shaker three times, each wash lasting 5 minutes.
Prepare 2% BSA blocking buffer by dissolving 2 g BSA powder in 100 ml PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20.
Remove PBS and add 200 μl of blocking buffer to block the rings for 1 hour at room temperature on an orbital shaker.
Aspirate the blocking buffer from each well.
Incubate each ring with 200 μl of primary antibody solution in blocking buffer, ensuring proper dilution according to instructions.
Remove the primary antibody solution from the rings.
Wash the rings with phosphate-buffered saline/tween (PBST) four times, each wash for 20 min at room temperature on an orbital shaker.
Add 200 μl per well of secondary antibody diluted in blocking buffer to the rings.
Wrap the 24-well plate in aluminum foil and store it at 4°C overnight on an orbital shaker.
Remove the secondary antibody from the rings.
Wash the rings with PBST four times, each wash for 20 min at room temperature on an orbital shaker.
Stain the cells with DAPI for 20–30 min at room temperature on an orbital shaker.
Discard the DAPI and wash the rings at least once with PBST to remove excess DAPI.
Image the stained rings on an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Image rings on inverted epifluorescence microscope.
Collect Z-stack images for each ring at 100 μm thickness and 2 μm step size.
Optimize exposure times based on negative controls (no primary antibody incubation).
Project 3D z-stacks to 2D using FIJI and the Extended Depth of Field plugin.
Use AngioTool to calculate total vessel growth per image area.
Use AngioTool to calculate average vessel length.
Save images as false-color JPEG for compatibility with AngioTool software.
Use JaCoP in FIJI to determine Pearson’s coefficient for specific markers with BON cells.
